text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm drafting a small change to the candidate-prioritization endpoint API. Want quick opinions before I open a PR.

maya: Short summary: 1) response uses a stable, monotonic `score` (float) rather than forcing calibrated probabilities, 2) add explicit `score_type` field in responses, 3) clarify billing units (scored_vs_returned), 4) allow an optional `X-Model-Affinity` header for routing hints + fallback list.

joel: Why not keep probabilities? Downstreams expect them.

rachel: probabilities imply calibration. We don't have tools to guarantee that across models/quantizations. Better to expose ordering and let teams handle normalization if they need it.

ben: We also need to be clear about units. If we score 100 candidates and return top-10, are we charging for 100 or 110? My vote: charge for candidates_scored only. Returning is cheap.

maya: Agreed re: units. Proposed billing calculation: `units_charged = candidates_scored` (optional extra cost for reranking with explainers). Will add a `billing` subfield in telemetry.

joel: Concern: breaking change for dashboards that show mean probability. Console will need to surface `score_type` and a migration guide.

maya: Example response I want in the spec:

```
{
  "score_type": "relative", // one of ["relative","logit","probability"]
  "scores": [
    {"id": "c_423", "score": -2.314},
    {"id": "c_87",  "score": 0.121}
  ],
  "meta": {"model_variant": "bert-large-v2"}
}
```

rachel: +1 to explicit `score_type`. Also telemetry should record `model_variant` and `score_type` for every request so we can track drift. Add `candidates_scored` and `units_charged` in traces.

ben: For routing: if client supplies `X-Model-Affinity: preferred=bert-large;fallback=bert-small,distil` we should try preferred if capacity, otherwise pick first available fallback. Record `fallback_reason` enum: ["no_capacity","degraded_perf","maintenance"].

maya: Good. Also runtime note: because we rely on continuous batching, absolute reproducibility might vary across runs. We should include `trace_id` and `seed_hash` in the response meta when `debug=true` so clients can correlate.

joel: UX/rollout idea: roll this behind a server-side feature flag `candidate_api_v2`. Console should show per-route toggle and opt-in percentage. When disabled, platform returns `score_type: "probability"` and old numeric scale.

rachel: Telemetry fields to emit: `score_type`, `model_variant`, `route_used`, `fallback_reason` (nullable), `candidates_scored`, `units_charged`, `latency_ms`, `request_size`. We should add dashboard widgets: score_type split, units_charged histogram, fallback heatmap.

ben: Also propose a per-customer quota rule: `max_scored_per_min` and a soft limit that returns `429` with body {"error":"quota_exceeded","quota": "scored_per_min"}. Console should show current usage vs quota at route level.

maya: Implementation checklist I will put in the PR: spec doc, schema change, runtime unit test (consistency across batches), billing hook, telemetry events, console flag + migration page, rollout plan.

joel: One more: clients sometimes persist scores and compare across days; we should explicitly recommend storing rank or re-scoring, not raw scores, since sign/scale changes across model variants. Add that to docs.

rachel: I'll take console/graphs. ben can do billing/quotas & telemetry. Maya if you can write the spec I'll review and open PR.

ben: :+1:

deploy-bot: deploy queued for feature-flag infra (ticket #INF-2189).

maya: Thanks all — will send a short RFC and link the PR later today.
